title: Lord, in the Strength of Grace
description: Lord, in the Strength of Grace in Tonic Solfa to AYLESBURY, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. His brother John printed them in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 426.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Short Metre (6.6.8.6), and this page sets them to AYLESBURY; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lord, in the strength of grace, With a glad heart and free, My-self, my re-si-due of days, I con-se-crate to thee.

lines: Lord, in the strength of grace,
With a glad heart and free,
And, from this moment, live or die

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to AYLESBURY by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
